findings.title: Production D06B cannot consume SourceRetriever’s return contract
findings.criterion_ref: RC9-T05 requires SourceRetriever retrieval, validation, hashing, and receipt creation before admission; RC9-T10 requires tests to exercise the production call site; RC9-T12 requires an executable route through N90.
findings.trigger: A real M01 discovery supplies a valid locator and production D06B calls the SourceRetriever created by build_runtime_context.
findings.consequence: SourceRetriever returns a `(body, receipt)` tuple, but D06B requires a mapping with `sha256`, `status`, and `content_type`. Every successful production retrieval therefore becomes SYSTEM_FAILURE before any retrieval record or interpretation packet can be admitted.
findings.evidence: runtime/langgraph_factory/egress.py lines 513–519 declare the tuple return, with receipt fields `bytes_sha256` and `http_status`; nodes/sources.py lines 406 and 419–433 treat the return as a mapping with different field names. test_plan26_deterministic_nodes.py lines 433–450 labels its stub “real-shaped” but only mirrors the call signature and returns the invented mapping D06B expects. A read-only probe combining the actual classes produced `SYSTEM_FAILURE/schema_contract: retrieval response ... must be a JSON object`.

findings.title: Redirect limits and HTTPS policy are checked only after redirects execute
findings.criterion_ref: RC9-T07 requires HTTPS and redirect bounds to be enforced at every hop; RC9-T10 requires genuine redirect-denial proof.
findings.trigger: An allowlisted host returns more than three same-host HTTPS redirects, or redirects to `http://<same-host>:443`.
findings.consequence: The default urllib opener follows the redirects while the retrieval grant is active. The configured redirect maximum is checked only after the final response, so excess requests already occurred. Per-hop validation checks only the hostname, allowing a same-host, same-port HTTP downgrade if that endpoint responds.
findings.evidence: runtime/langgraph_factory/egress.py lines 452–465 records redirects while delegating immediately to urllib; lines 553–566 perform the redirect-count and hostname-only checks after `_opener` returns and never recheck each hop’s scheme. tests/runtime/test_plan26_egress.py lines 307–336 use a canned, already-completed RetrievalResponse, so they do not exercise the production redirect-following call site or redirect bound.

findings.title: Responses with no Content-Type are admitted
findings.criterion_ref: RC9-T07 requires response type limits to fail closed.
findings.trigger: An otherwise authorized HTTP 200 response omits the Content-Type header.
findings.consequence: Arbitrary untyped bytes are hashed and recorded as an allowed source retrieval instead of being denied by the allowed-content-type policy.
findings.evidence: runtime/langgraph_factory/egress.py lines 572–574 rejects only when `content_type` is nonempty; lines 576–590 then append an allowed receipt with `content_type: null`. A read-only probe returned `outcome=allowed, content_type=None`. The tests cover a disallowed present header but no missing-header case.

observations: The submitted bundle hash and all listed live-file hashes matched, including the restored v7 and separately preserved modified-v7 bytes.

The active validator returned valid:true; the package suite reproduced 175 passes, N20 reproduced 489 passes plus one skip and 140 subtests, and N30 reproduced 62 passes plus 27 subtests. Those green results do not cover RC9-QA-001’s real component boundary.
The baseline live and `git show HEAD` hashes both matched the stated `9ce7fe5b...` value.
Some validator and test docstrings still say v7/results-v7, but their executable constants and assertions bind to graph v8/results-v8; this is nonfunctional wording drift.

The default opener reads the complete response before applying max_bytes. Oversized responses are rejected if the read completes, so I did not promote this to another finding, but streaming enforcement would prevent memory exhaustion.
reasoning: Hash, versioning, topology, ownership, policy-profile, model-assignment, validator, scanner, and baseline claims recomputed successfully. The verdict fails because the actual SourceRetriever-to-D06B boundary is unconditionally incompatible, while the passing test substitutes a different return contract. Independent per-hop redirect and missing-content-type conditions also defeat the explicit retrieval-security criterion.
